project_type: Next.js 16 admin dashboard (TypeScript/React) plus ~65 Python 3.12 AWS Lambda functions under amplify/functions/**. This task touches only the Python Lambdas and the Python test suite.
language: Python 3.12 for the work in this task (TypeScript elsewhere in the repo, not touched)
build_system: No Python build step. The Lambdas are plain source trees deployed as zips by scripts/deploy_all_lambdas.py (DO NOT RUN for this task). Use the repo virtualenv interpreter .venv/bin/python for everything Python; the system python3 does not have boto3. npm scripts (npm run build / lint / typecheck / test) are for the Next.js app and are irrelevant here.
test_framework: pytest. pytest.ini sets addopts=--import-mode=importlib and testpaths = tests, amplify/functions. conftest.py at the repo root has an autouse fixture that deletes sys.modules['handler'] between tests, because every Lambda entry point in the repo is named handler.py. Any test that needs a specific handler must load it by file path under a unique module name via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location - see tests/test_own_prefill_triggers_menu.py and tests/test_one_menu.py for the exact pattern, including the sys.path inserts for amplify/functions/shared, the handler dir, and its modules dir.
build_command: none for Python; syntax check with: .venv/bin/python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('<path>', encoding='utf-8').read())"
test_command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q   (full Python suite); .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q for the bare invocation that also collects amplify/functions/**
verification_instructions: 1) Run `git status --short` as its OWN command (never chained) before staging anything, and leave alone any modified file not in your owned-path list. 2) Syntax-check each edited handler with ast.parse. 3) Load each edited handler by file path with boto3.resource and boto3.client patched, and confirm it imports without raising. 4) Run the focused tests for the files you touched, then `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` for the whole Python suite. 5) Commit with `git add <new files> && git commit --only <explicit paths> -F <message-file>` - `--only` is MANDATORY on this task because a concurrent session committed to inbound-whatsapp-handler/handler.py during planning and the shared index may hold work that is not ours. 6) Never deploy: no scripts/deploy_all_lambdas.py, no scripts/snapstart_publish.py, no aws lambda update-function-code, no alias move, no Lambda deletion.
environment_constraints: Both handlers sit behind a Lambda `live` alias, so nothing in this change reaches production until a version is published and the alias moves - which this task forbids. The menus therefore remain live on both WABAs after this work lands; say so in the final report. The wd_menu WhatsApp template was DELETED at Meta by the owner, so any send referencing it fails now. Use .scratch/ (gitignored) for throwaway files, never /tmp. Secrets must never appear on a command line. Do not run `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value`.
contribution_requirements: Single-branch workflow: commit directly to `stack`, never create a feature branch, never force push, never rewrite history. Stage by explicit path and use `git commit --only` (see .kiro/steering/multi-session-parallel-agents.md rules 3, 3a, 3b - rule 3b was written after two separate incidents where a session swept another session's files into its commit). Never `git add .` / `-A` / `-u`. Commit messages describe what and why.
key_patterns: Plain-text outbound from the inbound handler goes through _send_ai_auto_reply(contact_id, text, phone_number_id, request_id), which async-invokes OUTBOUND_WHATSAPP_FUNCTION with a JSON body containing contactId/content/phoneNumberId. Interactive sends set isInteractive/interactiveType in the same payload. In whatsapp-calling, Meta Graph sends go through _meta_api_call(f'{meta_id}/messages', 'POST', payload, phone_number_id=meta_id); a reaction's message_id must belong to the SAME meta_id that produced it (documented at _react_thumbs_up), which is why the replacement text send must also use _meta_api_call rather than _send_via_aws. Logging masks phone numbers to the last four via mask_phone / mask_contact_id; a menu row id is NOT a secret and is logged in full. Keyword sets in the inbound handler are function-local and exact-match, with strip_decorative_edges() as a fallback.
directory_structure: amplify/functions/messaging/* holds one directory per messaging Lambda, each with handler.py (inbound-whatsapp-handler also has modules/content.py). amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ holds shared helpers importable by every function. tests/ holds the Python suite. scripts/ holds deploy and audit tooling (not used here). .kiro/steering/ holds the mandatory workspace rules. .scratch/ is gitignored scratch space.
critical_finding: Commit ed1f3911 ('Remove the WhatsApp interactive menu (empty DEFAULT_ONE_MENU sections)') landed on stack from a CONCURRENT session during planning. It emptied DEFAULT_ONE_MENU['sections'] and rewrote tests/test_one_menu.py, but left MENU_TO_KEYWORD, the retired menus, the submenu branches, the language picker and every wd_menu send in place. Because _send_interactive_list short-circuits on an empty sections list (handler.py:5009), a greeting currently produces TOTAL SILENCE - the exact outcome this task forbids. All line numbers in plan.md were re-derived against ed1f3911 by AST walk, but re-derive again with `.venv/bin/python .scratch/menu_extents.py` before editing, and treat the git index as potentially dirty with another session's work.
